stemMd: While pure ice melts at its melting point under constant pressure, added heat mainly does what?

options.label: B
options.textMd: Changes phase while temperature remains approximately constant until melting is complete

options.label: D
options.textMd: Converts oxygen nuclei into hydrogen nuclei

options.label: E
options.textMd: Raises the temperature of all remaining ice immediately above the melting point

explanationMd: At the melting point, energy is used to change intermolecular arrangement rather than raise temperature during the phase transition. This is latent heat, distinct from sensible heating within one phase.

distractorRationale.e: During coexistence the added energy mainly supplies latent heat.
distractorRationale.a: Phase change conserves mass in a closed system.
